name: Miriam
bio:
Miriam is the daughter of Amram and Jochebed, the elder sister of Moses and Aaron, and one of the women in Scripture specifically called a "prophetess" (Exodus 15:20). When the infant Moses was set adrift on the Nile in a basket, it was Miriam who watched from a distance, and after Pharaoh's daughter discovered the baby, she cleverly stepped forward to suggest that Moses' own mother serve as his nurse — allowing him to be raised under his birth mother's care (Exodus 2:4-8).

After Israel crossed the Red Sea and escaped the pursuing Egyptians, Miriam took up a timbrel and led the women in dancing, singing, "Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea" — one of the earliest recorded scenes of a woman leading worship in Scripture (Exodus 15:20-21). Miriam appears further in Israel's wilderness journey, including the account in Numbers 12 where she and Aaron opposed Moses over his Cushite wife, and she was struck with leprosy as a result.
